tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Search apps on the Apple App Store, Google Play, or both. Returns matching apps with store, title, developer, icon, price, rating, category, and url. Use store="both" to fan out to both engines and merge results. Apple limit is clamped to 50; Google supports 1-250. The price filter (free/paid) only

tools.name: get_apps_batch
tools.description: Resolve a single Apple app by bundleId (e.g. com.burbn.instagram), or fetch many apps at once with a comma-separated ids batch (Apple up to ~200 ids in one round-trip; Google fans out and coalesces). A batch request returns an "apps" array; a bundleId request returns a single "app". Supports store="

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Full details for one app: description, version, release dates, content rating, genres, screenshots, languages, rating (with histogram and current-version stats), version history, size, installs, IAP flag, privacy policy, and store-specific extras. {id} is the Apple trackId (numeric string, e.g. 6448

tools.name: get_app_reviews
tools.description: Reviews for one app. Apple reviews come from the customerreviews RSS feed and are hard-capped at 500 per app per country (50/page x pages 1-10); page>10 returns an error, and sort="rating" is not supported for Apple. Google reviews are token-paginated and effectively unbounded — pass the nextToken f

tools.name: get_similar_apps
tools.description: "Customers also bought" / related apps for one app. First-class on both stores.

tools.name: get_app_permissions
tools.description: Google Play declared device/data permissions for one app, grouped by permission group. Google only — passing store="apple" returns a not_supported error.

tools.name: get_app_datasafety
tools.description: Google Play "Data safety" section for one app: data shared, data collected, security practices, and privacy policy URL. Google only — passing store="apple" returns a not_supported error.

tools.name: get_charts
tools.description: Ranked top-chart entries (App summary plus rank) for a store. type is free/paid/grossing (Apple also supports new/newfree/newpaid). category is an Apple genre id (e.g. 6007) or a Google category constant (e.g. PRODUCTIVITY); omit for the overall chart. Google list() may return an empty array with me

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: List categories for a store. Apple returns its static 6000/7000-range genre map; Google returns its categories() constants.

tools.name: get_developer
tools.description: A developer record plus their published apps. {id} is the Apple artistId (numeric) or the Google developerId string (e.g. "Google LLC").

tools.name: autocomplete_suggest
tools.description: Up to 5 autocomplete completions for a partial search query. First-class on both stores.

tools.name: get_aso_keywords
tools.description: Directional keyword ideas for a seed term, each with a difficulty score/label, traffic score, result count, and top competitors — derived from live search/suggest results, not panel data. Every result is labeled estimated:true.

tools.name: get_aso_rank
tools.description: Point-in-time rank of one app across up to 20 keywords (one live search per keyword, fan-out capped at 20). Every result is labeled estimated:true. This is a snapshot, not rank tracking over time.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_apps, get_app_reviews, get_app_datasafety · Private data: get_app_reviews, get_developer · Public sink: get_app_reviews.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_apps, get_app_reviews, get_app_datasafety · Private data: get_app_reviews, get_developer · Public sink: get_app_reviews

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
